extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans, students and researchers interested in Stephenie Meyer, Twilight, or YA vampire/paranormal romance
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article summarizing Stephenie Meyer's life, publications, writing style, themes, reception, adaptations, and cultural impact; useful as background and as a source of implicit style/quality criteria for YA/paranormal romance writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use active voice and front-load information
rubrics_metrics.description: Meyer relies on detailed expository descriptions and active voice in her novels; she often opens her sentences with the most important information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a stylistic signature: prefer active constructions and put key info early in sentences. Useful for direct, readable prose; may contribute to perceived simplicity or bluntness if overused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show rather than tell (avoid excessive telling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics say Meyer 'relied too much on "telling" rather than "showing"' and that this contributes to amateurish or overearnest writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer scenes that dramatize rather than summarise characters' emotions and motivations; reduce expository summarizing of feelings. Excessive telling can lead to weaker reader engagement and critical remarks about writing craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid repetitive, overearnest phrasing ('jackhammer' repetition)
rubrics_metrics.description: NPR criticized Twilight as a repetitive 'jackhammer' masked behind ornate language; The New York Times called parts 'overearnest, amateurish writing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for repeated words, phrases, or rhetorical effects that fatigue the reader; ornamental language should not be used to hide repetitiveness or thin plotting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit predictable focus on physical attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: Corpus analysis found much description and characterization revolves around physical attributes such as eyes, face, expression, and frequent words like 'black' and 'dark', producing predictability and superficiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversify descriptive strategies beyond recurrent physical features; avoid templates that repeatedly foreground the same physical details, which can make characterization feel shallow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt an appropriate melodramatic/YA paranormal-romance tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Meyer's work is typically classified as melodrama and is positioned within vampire romance / young adult / paranormal romance genres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If writing for the same market, expect heightened emotion, romantic focus, and genre conventions (e.g., supernatural romance). Tone should match audience expectations while managing potential critical responses to melodrama.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid graphic sexual content in YA-targeted stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Meyer was adamant against including graphic sex in her Twilight series; lack of sex and eroticizing abstinence contributed to the series' appeal to some readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For YA romance, limit explicit sexual description; sexual tension and abstinence can be used as narrative devices, but balance with honest portrayal of relationships and consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreground themes of agency, mortality, temptation, and eternal life
rubrics_metrics.description: Themes consistent with Meyer's religion — agency, mortality, temptation, and eternal life — are prominent in her work and shape character arcs and moral choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed recurring moral/spiritual themes in plot and character development; explore characters' choices, temptations, and consequences in ways that serve story and character growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use intertextual allusions to canonical literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Meyer makes allusions to canonical texts (e.g., Book of Genesis, Wuthering Heights, Macbeth, Pride and Prejudice, Shakespeare) and ties books in the series to specific classics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allusions can enrich themes and resonance; ensure they are purposeful and accessible to the intended readership rather than gratuitous name-dropping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize detailed character description to foster reader identification (intentional sparseness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Meyer has stated she intentionally avoided describing her characters in detail, which she believes allows the reader to more easily 'step into [their] shoes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberate minimalism in physical or internal description can increase reader projection/identification, but may reduce distinctiveness; balance minimal detail with enough specificity to make characters feel alive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use paratext (chapter titles) to convey inner life when prose is reserved
rubrics_metrics.description: In New Moon, Meyer offers 'deeper insight into Bella's psyche' through the chapter titles, rather than the prose itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter titles or other paratextual elements can provide psychological or thematic framing when the prose keeps interiority understated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research and responsibly represent real-world cultures (avoid cultural appropriation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Meyer researched the Quileute Native Americans to include their legends and traditions, though some tribe members found her use offensive; the Quileute described her use of their traditions and merchandising as cultural theft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When incorporating real cultural legends/traditions, consult with communities, fact-check representations, avoid stereotyping or commodification, and respect cultural sensitivities and intellectual property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid romanticizing abusive or retrogressive gender roles; preserve female agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholars and critics have accused the series of romanticizing a physically abusive relationship and promoting retrogressive gender stereotypes; criticisms focus on Bella's dependence and limited autonomy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray relationships and gender roles with attention to agency, consent, and power dynamics; center character choice and avoid glamorizing dependency or abusive patterns without critical framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain coherent point-of-view (POV) choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics noted that Breaking Dawn's narrative shifts and the decision to change POV (e.g., briefly to Jacob) contributed to chaotic or uneven reception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POV shifts should serve clear narrative purposes; abrupt or poorly signaled changes can confuse readers and undermine narrative coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage internet and fan engagement for readership and marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: The success of the Twilight series has been attributed to the Internet, which allowed Meyer to directly reach fans; early bimonthly book signings helped cultivate her fanbase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use online platforms, author-fan interaction, and in-person events to build community and momentum. These strategies can amplify commercial success even when critical reception is mixed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use music playlists or external media to shape tone and scene emotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Meyer cites music as a prominent influence on her writing and posts playlists of songs that specifically inspired her books; she used different music to influence genres of scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creating playlists or using other media as emotional/reference tools can help maintain consistent tone and inspire scene-level choices during drafting.
